companions.name: M4 V69 B
companions.description: The secondary star of the eclipsing binary M4 V69, 0.7278 solar masses and 0.8074 solar radii; the two stars eclipse each other every 48.188 days.

radius.source: Secondary radius (solar radii) 0.8074 +/- 0.008, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K)

mass.source: Secondary mass (solar masses) 0.7278 +/- 0.0048, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K)

temperature.source: Secondary log Teff 3.772 +/- 0.01, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K): 5916 K

orbit.source: M4 V69: P 48.1882687 d and primary-eclipse time HJD 2450048.3489 (Section II, text before Equation (1)); i 89.789 degrees (Table 11, column V69 (third)); e 0.384, omega 65.25 degrees (Table 10, column V69); checked: with it as published the companion is straight behind within 0.07 h of the published secondary eclipse at phase 0.6086052 (Table 3 footnote); +180 degrees would miss by 72 h. HJD is taken as BJD_TDB (under a minute apart); at the primary eclipse the secondary is in front, the component these papers call primary being the one eclipsed at phase 0. Separation from Kepler's third law with DEBCat's masses

text.card: The secondary star of M4 V69, a pair that eclipse each other every 48.188 days.
text.introduction: It has 0.7278 solar masses and 0.8074 solar radii; its partner has 0.7665 and 0.8655, measured from the eclipses and the stars' motions.
text.locator: DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164), M4 V69: Mass, Radius and Period, from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K)
